page.intro: ECharts measures its container when it draws and never again on its own. Each context below draws the same series twice -- once as ipecharts mounts it, once with the app telling it its box changed -- so you can see which layouts need telling. Measured on this page: only two of the seven do. The headings say which, and why.

column.title: 1. A plain page column — fine
column.description: The control case. Nothing changes this chart's width except the browser window, and a window resize is one of the events ipecharts already listens for. Resize the window: both charts follow.

width.title: 2. A container that changes width — BREAKS
width.description: The card goes from half width to full width with no window resize, so nothing asks the chart to measure again and it keeps its old canvas. The second chart is told, but only after a pause: a nudge sent in the same batch as the layout change redraws at the old width, because the browser has not applied the new one yet.

panel.title: 3. Inside a collapsed panel — fine
panel.description: This one looks dangerous and is not. Vuetify does not mount a collapsed panel's content, so the chart is built the moment you open it, when its container already has a width.

tabs.title: 4. On a tab nobody has opened — fine
tabs.description: The same story one layer up: the second tab's content is mounted the first time it is shown, not with the page, so the chart never measures a hidden box.
tabs.first_body: Switch to the second tab: the chart is built now, not when this page loaded.

right_panel.title: 5. MapApp's right panel — fine
right_panel.description: Closing the panel slides it out of view without changing its width, so the chart inside keeps a box it can still trust. The app watches MapApp's own traits anyway, which is what a panel that did change width would need.

panel.title: Charts
panel.description: Contexts 5 to 7 live here. Open and close this panel, open the dialog step, and open the chart button on the map: the chart on the map is the one that mounts inside an already-rendered menu, so it measures a hidden box and starts out wrong.
